newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to continue reconstruction - Hariri.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to continue reconstruction - Hariri.

text.p: Lebanon will continue its reconstruction drive and the development of its capital markets despite the stagnation of the Arab-Israeli peace process, Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri told Arab bankers on Wednesday.

Apparently responding to frequent criticism that the success of the ambitious programme he launched in 1992 was tied to the success of the peace process, Hariri said he would not allow Lebanon's power of decision to be mortgaged to Israel's will.

"Now, since peace has not been reached because of Israeli obstinacy, the position of the Lebanese government is that we must go on in our development programmes," Hariri told a Beirut conference on Arab Capital Markets.
Lebanon would continue "to attract capital, to be open to international markets and to attract Lebanese and Arab capital to invest in Lebanon", he said in a speech.
The election of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a year ago had caused problems for Israel but would not become a problem for Arab countries, Hariri said.
"As you see, Israel now suffers isolation while the Arab countries are in solidarity with each other for the sake of peace," he said.
"We believe in peace but we did not bet on peace because such a bet means we are pledging our national and political decision to the other party with whom we want to make peace.
"We will not put our political decision in Israel's hands. We will continue our reconstruction programme," Hariri declared.
